title: Service impersonation via session TTL boundary causing incorrect audit annotations
creator: Maya Patel
description: Customer reported intermittent instances where actions performed by a delegated service principal appeared in the audit logs as if executed by a different higher-privileged admin user. Investigation shows correlation with SAML session refreshes, group-sync events, and RBAC v2 role resolution happening across a TTL boundary. This ticket tracks the bug, mitigation, and rollout to prevent over-permissioned activity attribution and to preserve correct audit annotations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure SAML IdP with group membership sync every 5 minutes and map admin-group to 'org.admin' role via RBAC v2 mapping rules.
2) Create a long-lived service principal that uses delegate flow and inherits roles from the group's assertion during login.
3) Trigger a group membership change on IdP (add service principal to admin-group) then cause a session refresh around the 5-minute window (simulate clock drift ~30s).
4) Observe audit log entries for subsequent actions and cross-check 'actor' and 'effective_roles' fields in the audit events.

5) Intermittent events show 'actor' as the human admin user from stale session context instead of the service principal; at the same time 'effective_roles' shows admin privileges for the service principal.
6) Reproduce more reliably by accelerating group-sync and forcing concurrent role-resolution requests during a session refresh (load test harness attached).
suspected_root_cause: Race between SAML assertion processing (session refresh) and RBAC v2 role cache invalidation. When a human admin's session is refreshed and a service principal is added to an admin group almost concurrently, the async role-resolution path can attach the wrong session identity to the token that carries elevated roles. Audit annotation code path relied on a later identity lookup that occasionally read from stale session-mapping cache, resulting in mismatched 'actor' metadata despite correct 'effective_roles'.
proposed_fix: 1) Make session-to-actor binding atomic during SAML assertion handling: attach immutable session_id and actor_id to the token before any async role resolution. 2) Change RBAC v2 cache invalidation to emit a deterministic event that blocks token-issue path briefly (~50ms) when group membership deltas are detected for affected identities. 3) Add end-to-end unit tests and integration tests that exercise the session-refresh + group-sync race. 4) Add an audit log field 'session_consistency_version' to help detect future anomalies.
implementation_notes: - Add session_id binding in saml/service_auth.go:BindSessionAndActor (atomic commit), fallback to reject token issuance if binding cannot be acquired.

- Modify rbac/cache.go to support per-identity generation counters; when a sync delta arrives bump generation and block token issuance for that identity until generation sync completes or timeout (50ms).
- Update audit/annotator.go to include 'session_consistency_version' and ensure 'actor' is resolved synchronously from token's bound actor_id.
- Ensure zero-downtime rollout by using feature-flag 'rbac-session-atomic-binding' for a staged rollout and telemetry gating.
testing_plan: Unit tests for session binding and rbac generation bump; integration scenario in staging with IdP simulator shim to control sync timing; synthetic load test that reproduces race; canary rollout to <10% of traffic, observe audit mismatch rates on dashboard (grafana panel: security.rbac.audit_mismatch_rate).
rollback_plan: If canary increases error rate or causes auth latency >50ms p95, flip 'rbac-session-atomic-binding' feature-flag to off; revert rbac cache change via hotfix branch.
incident_timeline: 2026-03-03: Customer (Acme Analytics) opened priority support case describing suspicious admin-level writes attributed to 'alice@example.com' while service principal performed writes.
2026-03-04: Pager duty triggered. Initial mitigation: temporary removal of service principal from admin-group at customer request.
2026-03-07: Reproduced locally with IdP simulator; collected audit logs showing mismatch in actor vs effective_roles.
2026-03-09: Implemented prototype that pins actor_id to token; local tests reduced mismatch from 1.9% to 0.0% in synthetic run.
2026-03-10: Create ticket ENG-65521 and assign to security infra squad; customer notified of patch schedule.
mitigation: Short term: block all long-lived delegated tokens from being granted admin-group derived privileges until patched (telemetry-based hold). Applied a CI rule to fail deployments that create new delegated admin tokens. Communicated temporary policy to affected customers.
observability_changes: Add grafana panels: security.rbac.audit_mismatch_rate, security.rbac.session_binding_failures, security.rbac.token_issue_latency. Emit metric rbac.session_binding_block_ms to monitor blocking window.
notes: This bug differs from prior 'role shadowing' reports: root cause is session/actor binding race rather than stale RBAC policy cache alone. Adding consistency version to audit events will make future post-mortems faster. Coordinate with SRE to ensure a 50ms blocking window doesn't cascade under high auth load.
